practice1.prompt: write letter_grade so all four assertions in the test class hold

cases.name: 80 is a B, not a C

hiddenCases.name: 90 is the bottom of the A band

practice1.hint: assertRaises is asking the function to refuse, not to return a grade for nonsense. Check the range first, then work down the bands -- and note that every boundary in the list is itself a pass into the band above it.

questions.prompt: Match each unittest method to what it checks.
right: A value is somewhere in a collection
The call throws the exception you named
questions.explain: Each assertion says a different kind of thing. Reaching for assertTrue when you mean assertEqual costs you the failure message that would have told you both values.

questions.prompt: Why does assertRaises take the function and its arguments separately, rather than a call?
choices: So unittest can make the call itself inside a place where it can catch the exception
It is a historical accident with no reason
questions.explain: If you called it yourself the exception would escape before assertRaises ever saw it. Handing over the function and its arguments lets unittest run it under a guard.

questions.prompt: What does it mean that a TestCase method must start with the word test?
choices: It is a style convention only
unittest finds and runs methods by that prefix, so one without it is never run
Python requires the prefix on all methods
It controls the order they run in
questions.explain: A helper method inside a TestCase is useful and deliberately not run. The consequence is that a typo in the prefix produces a test that silently never runs and never fails.

questions.prompt: The four assertions in the lesson pin 95, 80, 12 and 130. Which behaviours are left unpinned by those four?
questions.explain: The four cases cover an A, a B, an F and one refusal. Every boundary between them, and the other end of the range, is a decision the suite has no opinion about.

reflection-exercise1.hint: Say what unittest gives you that a file of loose asserts does not: grouping, running them all, and telling you which failed.

reflection-exercise2.hint: A class holding methods whose names begin with test. Say why the prefix matters -- a method without it is never run.
